summary: In civil government and space policy, President Donald Trump has signed an executive order establishing a U.S. Space Academy and awarded NASA’s Artemis II crew the Congressional Space Medal of Honor. In commercial launch and operations, SpaceX recovered its Starship spacecraft from the Indian Ocean to ship it back to Texas following a test flight, a European Ariane 6 rocket successfully launched a weather satellite into orbit, and a private Chinese rocket experienced an explosive first landing attempt. On the military front, a new report reveals the U.S. Space Force spent $124 million on commercial data and services over nearly three years, while the service branch adopted a digital engineering tool for its NC3 satellite program and awarded LeoLabs a $20.68 million contract. Internationally, NASA invited media to an upcoming ceremony where Turkey will sign the Artemis Accords. In space science, planetary researchers determined that Mercury’s crust points to deeper, hotter volcanic origins than previously expected, while NASA confirmed its Swift space telescope will crash back to Earth following the failure of a private rescue mission. Looking ahead, observers should watch for the planned August 30 launch of NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket.
